title: Comma-Separated Employee List Per Department
description:
For each department produce a single comma-separated list of employee names sorted alphabetically.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `department`

Output columns: `department`, `employee_list`, `headcount`. Order by `department`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineering'),(2,'Bob','Engineering'),(3,'Carol','Engineering'),(4,'Dave','Marketing'),(5,'Eve','Marketing'),(6,'Frank','HR'),(7,'Grace','HR'),(8,'Henry','HR');
solution_sql: SELECT department, STRING_AGG(name, ', ' ORDER BY name) AS employee_list, COUNT(*) AS headcount FROM employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY department

test_cases.description: 3 departments: Engineering (3 employees), HR (3 employees), Marketing (2 employees)

hints: STRING_AGG(name, ', ' ORDER BY name) concatenates all names in the group with ', ' as the separator in alphabetical order.
MySQL uses GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name SEPARATOR ', ') — STRING_AGG is the standard SQL / PostgreSQL / DuckDB syntax.
explanation: STRING_AGG is an aggregate function that collects values into a delimited string. GROUP BY department produces one row per department. Engineering: 'Alice, Bob, Carol'. HR: 'Frank, Grace, Henry'. Marketing: 'Dave, Eve'. headcount from COUNT(*) is included to verify the list length matches.
